newsitem.title: UK: Scandalous British marriage records auctioned.
newsitem.headline: Scandalous British marriage records auctioned.

text.p: A century's worth of records logging scandalous, secretive and forbidden marriages performed in the Scottish village of Gretna Green fetched 11,500 pounds ($18,990) at auction on Thursday.
The records were bought within two minutes of bidding by the Institute of Heraldic and Genealogical Studies in Canterbury, southern England.
"We wanted to buy the collection to keep it together and in this country, rather than being split up and in private hands," said Liz Bregazzi, an agent acting on behalf of the Institute.

Gretna Green, a village on the Scottish border, became a haven for eloping couples after a 1754 bill outlawed unlicensed marriage in England in order to prevent young heiresses being abducted and forced into marriage.
The Scottish village was the 19th century's answer to Las Vegas, requiring only that couples declare their wish to marry before witnesses.

"This is the first time records such as these have been auctioned on the open market. They are the earliest records of marriages from Gretna Green in existence," said Andrew McCoull of the auction house Anderson and Garland in Newcastle upon Tyne, northern England.
The collection included six marriage registers, 21 bundles of loose records plus invoices and other documents covering hasty marriages struck between 1794 and 1874.
The records trace the marriages conducted by three generations of the Lang family, the most famous of the "priests" who married couples after they fled across the border.
One of the more scandalous Gretna Green matches was that of former lord chancellor Thomas Erskine, 68, who ran away with his young housekeeper, mother to his illegitimate child, in 1818.

Another Lang marriage resulted in a sensational trial after bridegroom Edward Gibbon-Wakefield abducted a wealthy 15-year-old heiress from her boarding school in 1826 before marrying her in Gretna Green.
He and his accomplice were sentenced to three years in jail.
